title: Building a square wave from sines
sub: Partial sums of (4/π)(sin x + sin 3x/3 + sin 5x/5 + …).

frames.caption: One sine wave, (4/π) sin x, is already a rough square wave (the flat steps, muted). The 4/π makes it the best single-sine fit.
Add (4/3π) sin 3x (aqua, the newest term). It pushes the shoulders up and the middle down, squaring off the shape.
Add sin 5x / 5. Each new odd harmonic is smaller, by 1/n, and wiggles faster.
5 terms, up to sin 9x: flatter tops and steeper edges. But look at the corners: the sum overshoots 1.
10 terms. Everywhere away from the jump the error is shrinking, but the overshoot near the jump is still there, about 0.18 above the step.
25 terms. The overshoot has moved closer to the jump (its peak sits at about π/(2N)) but it is no shorter.

60 terms. The peak is still at 1.177: the Gibbs phenomenon. The overshoot tends to about 1.179, roughly 9% of the full jump from −1 to 1, however many terms you add. It just gets squeezed into a narrower and narrower spike.
